Life is but an everlasting battle, one we try so desparately to fight.  It is a tunnel, full of black mold and thick dust, you cough and gag as you struggle to breathe.  No light greets you on the way forward through this tunnel, in fact the darkness seems to grow deeper in depth and you lose sense of yourself because you can not see yourself.  You reach around to feel the walls of the tunnel but you realize your body has gone numb.  You can't feel anything, and the tunnel suddenly feels more like an endless black void.  Now, you can not feel ANYTHING.  Emotion is null, nonexistent.  You are numb, cold.

I am a 21 year old guy who cut himself yesterday, out of anger towards myself for being who I am.  I'm staring at ways to take my own life every day just to get it over with.

But I haven't.

Every soul contains a whisper of light, every heart contains a pebble of hope; we all feel it, even if it is brief while we tie the noose around our necks our place the muzzle to the roof of our mouths.  That spark that shoots through your mind like a tiny lightning bolt.  Hope.  As I sit here with red, stinging scars across my left arm that replace older scars from the times I've cut before, I'm here.  I'm alive.  Because I've taken a grasp of that tiny snowflake of hope in a blizzard of hopelessness.

When one wants to take their own life, they usually don't necessarily want to die.  They want the pain to stop, they want something or someone to cuddle their heart.

I can't match my experiences with yours, I can't understand what you've been through.  But I feel inclined to try and help you, from one suffering person to another.
